chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id (Ibn 'Uqdah) said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazimi narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ali al-Murafiqi and Abu Ahmad 'Amr ibn al-Rabi' al-Nasri narrated to us from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him).

He was asked about recitation behind the Imam, so he said: 'If you are behind an Imam whom you follow and trust, then his recitation suffices for you. And if you wish to recite, then recite in what he recites quietly. When he recites loudly, then be silent.' Allah the Exalted said: 'And be silent, perhaps you will be shown mercy.'
He said: Then it was said to him: 'If I do not trust him, should I pray behind him and recite?' He said: 'Do not pray before him or after him.'

It was said to him: 'Should I pray behind him and make it a voluntary prayer?' He said: 'If the voluntary prayer were accepted, the obligatory prayer would be accepted, but make it a 'subhah' (silent recitation without loud recitation).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Quran behind the Imam if he is not trustworthy?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between reciting behind a trustworthy Imam, where the Imam's recitation suffices but quiet personal recitation is permitted, and a less trusted Imam, where the follower should render the obligatory prayer as a silent 'subhah' (voluntary/silent recitation) rather than reciting aloud. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that the validity of the prayer depends on the follower's confidence in the Imam's religious integrity, with the Imam citing the Quranic command to 'listen attentively' as the basis for silence during the Imam's loud recitation.
